The People and Instructions Behind Your Mother's Week, in One Place

A one-page inventory of the names, numbers and written instructions the family already has, and the ones nobody has.

Download PDF

The neighbor's number is in your sister's phone, the pharmacy's is on a pill bottle, and the note from the doctor's office is somewhere in the kitchen.

This page doesn't ask you to understand or judge any of it. It asks where each thing is, how recent it is, and who has it.

What to collectWhere it isIts dateWho has it
Names and phone numbers for everyone with a regular day: your sister, the neighbor, anyone else
Names and phone numbers for anyone who has said they could cover
Her doctor's office: name and phone number
Her pharmacy: name and phone number
Any other professional she sees regularly
Written instructions from her doctor or another professional
Her medication list, if one is written down
The family's own page of who helps and when, if there is one
Notes anyone has kept on things they've noticed

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

What's missing, and who will ask for it

Anything above with an empty line. Put a name next to each.

For example Only my sister has the neighbor's number. She'll send it to the rest of us. Nobody knows whether there's a written medication list; I'll ask her on Sunday.

How to use it

  • Ask your mother first. It's her doctor, her pharmacy and her neighbor, and she decides what gets shared and with whom.
  • For a phone number, the date is when someone last used it. For a paper, it's the date printed on it. If there isn't one, write “undated.”
  • Don't copy out or summarize an instruction here. Just say where it is.
  • Keep the page somewhere the family can find it, and tell everyone where that is.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't explain what any instruction means or whether it still applies. If something you find isn't clear, that's a question for the person who wrote it.
